officialTitle: Crizotinib in ROS1-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We enrolled 50 patients with advanced NSCLC who tested positive for ROS1 rearrangement in an expansion cohort of the phase 1 study of crizotinib.

clinicalQuestion: Does crizotinib have antitumour activity in advanced ROS1-rearranged NSCLC?

arms.label: Crizotinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were treated with crizotinib at the standard oral dose of 250 mg twice daily

publications.title: Crizotinib in ROS1-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer.
publications.label: ROS1 expansion cohort

outcomes.sourceQuote: The objective response rate was 72% (95% confidence interval [CI], 58 to 84), with 3 complete responses and 33 partial responses.
The median duration of response was 17.6 months (95% CI, 14.5 to not reached).
Median progression-free survival was 19.2 months (95% CI, 14.4 to not reached), with 25 patients (50%) still in follow-up for progression.

safety.sourceQuote: The safety profile of crizotinib was similar to that seen in patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC.

strengths: Molecularly defined cohort with fusion-partner characterisation

clinicalImplications.text: Defined ROS1 rearrangement as an actionable driver in NSCLC with high responsiveness to crizotinib, supporting routine ROS1 testing.

tumourBoardPearl.text: ROS1 shares kinase-domain homology with ALK — crizotinib was active across fusion partners.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 25264305.
